newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle end mostly up, feeders mixed.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle end mostly up, feeders mixed.

text.p: CME live cattle futures ended mostly higher as short covering from an oversold condition more than offset further fund selling, traders said.

"The break (in December) has been overdone to the downside in light of where cash is at" currently, said Doug Harper, senior livestock analyst for Brock Associates Inc. He noted that December already was at a large discount to current cash cattle prices which should cover the expected increase in cattle numbers going into the end of the year.
"Buying December live cattle anywhere close to $64 (per cwt) is going to be a pretty good position," he said.
Cash cattle sold at $70 per cwt in direct Plains trade Tuesday and October live cattle futures finished at 70.375 cents a lb while December ended at 64.700 cents.

October also rallied early on short covering but slipped again after midsession as recent fed cattle price weakness and long liquidation weighed on that month. Fed cattle prices slipped $1 this week despite currently tight market ready supplies, traders said.
Early estimates on Friday's monthly USDA Cattle-on-Feed report ranged from 93.8 to 97.0 percent of a year ago for on-feed cattle supplies at major feedlots.
Placement estimates were ranging from 96.2 to 104 percent of year-ago placements which were relatively large. Early marketing estimates ranged from 85 to 90.8 percent.
Dean Witter, E.D.& F. Man, Refco and Rand Financials bought December early while R.J. O'Brien, Dean Witter and E.D.&F. Man bought late, traders said, while Refco sold late.
In live cattle options, December volatility was down on selling of 54 puts. There was also new long positioning seen in February, buying of 64 calls and selling of 62 puts, pit sources added.

Feeder cattle futures followed the lead of live cattle but spreading and late renewed selling made for a mixed close. A lower trend to corn futures denoting easing feed costs also lent support, traders said.
"With corn cheaper there should be decent support under the feeder cattle," Harper said.
Spreading based on the lower feed costs accounted for much of the activity during the session, traders said.

Cargill notably spread long January feeders/short June live cattle and long November feeders/short April live cattle, traders said. Lind-Waldock and E.D.&F. Man bought December live cattle and sold January feeders, pit sources said.
Feeder cattle closed 0.150 cent a lb lower to 0.225 higher with November up 0.075 at 62.575 cents.
